records.mutation: diagnose all-candidates-refuted as an over-narrow list and require checking the degenerate equal/extremal case; ban reporting an already-refuted value
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 1/8; every rollout burned 14k-16.4k tokens and 2 truncated. Seven failures built only the factor-pair list of the displayed number, applied it to both readings, refuted every pair, and then reported one of those refuted factors anyway (or a value they called recalled or intended). The lone success was the only rollout that considered the balanced split into two equal parts, a candidate no factor list can reach. So I replaced the incumbent intersect-across-readings clause with a generic diagnosis: all-candidates-refuted means the list was too narrow, and the equal-or-extremal degenerate case must be added and checked. I also hardened the ban to cover reporting an already-refuted value and added a restatement tripwire to cut the token burn.

records.mutation: swap the incumbent's symmetry-axis circle shortcut for a representation rule: impose a pinned magnitude as one direct algebraic equation instead of parametrizing by an angle and eliminating trig
records.subagent_summary: All eight fresh rollouts were correct, so train is saturated at 1.0 while transfer sits at 0.175; length is where the evidence lives. Six finished in 5.7k-8.2k tokens by imposing the magnitude condition as a single algebraic equation in the coordinates, but the outlier ran to 14.6k because it parametrized by an angle and then fought to eliminate the trig, deriving three mutually inconsistent expressions for the cosine and spending thousands of tokens reconciling them before recovering. Rounds 5-8 all tried to manage or repair that self-contradiction loop after it starts and all lost transfer, so I instead remove the representation choice that creates it, and drop the seldom-used symmetry-axis clause to pay for the words.

records.mutation: diagnose the real truncation cause: replace the symmetry-wedge clause with a bound-plus-witness stop reason and a rule to transcribe (not re-derive) the settled numbers in the visible write-up
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts scored. Every failure was pure truncation, not a math error: all four reached the correct value inside the first ~4-7k of ~55-63k characters, then burned 100+ rotation re-tests and 50-82 restarts. Decisively, three of the four had already closed reasoning and were mid-way through a fresh from-scratch write-up (restating the problem, re-deriving the union identity, recomputing the overlap) when the cap hit, so the value never became visible; a fourth was cut off inside its own result markup. The incumbent's symmetry clause is spent, so this trims it and buys two things: a logical licence to halt (a universal bound plus an attaining configuration is already a proof), and an explicit instruction to transcribe the settled numbers rather than re-derive them after reasoning ends.

records.mutation: split the per-piece root cap from the whole-pattern cap and add a use-every-given-number audit against answering only the degree or only the piece count
records.subagent_summary: 3 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct. Every failure that finished mis-sized the cap in the same two ways: two applied the degree-d root bound to the entire pattern and reported the bare degree, and one insisted each term needs its own distinct object so answered the object count; two more truncated at the token limit while relooping on whether one object can step by a constant. The three successes all reached the summed disjoint-root budget. So the revision keeps the pointwise-residual and false-demand language that is clearly working and sharpens exactly the collapse point: it states that the degree-d bound caps ONE piece and not the pattern, and adds a short audit that the reported count must use every quantity the problem supplied, flagging a lone degree or a lone piece count as a dropped factor.

records.mutation: make the cross-check terminal: agreement freezes the value, later disagreement is the pass at fault, and ban speculating an intended value
records.subagent_summary: Five of eight fresh rollouts were correct. The most diagnostic failure had already reached the right value and cross-checked it by two routes, then re-derived it during write-up, botched one shoelace sign, and overrode its own confirmed result. The two other failures both hit the 16384-token cap: each reached a no-real-root contradiction, then spent the remaining budget guessing what value the problem 'must' intend instead of repairing the single bad rewrite. The incumbent's 'verify with a second, different method' clause is satisfied but has no stopping power, so I made confirmation terminal (agreement freezes the value; a later disagreeing pass is the error) and banned speculating about an intended value. This targets both self-override and budget death generically, and stays terse, since every rewrite above 100 tokens has lost transfer here.

records.mutation: name the uniform-random-permutation phrase as the trap (many-to-one step sequences, unreachable orderings) and make small-case enumeration a veto over any formula
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 1/8; six rollouts stopped normally at 9k-15k tokens and two hit the cap while relitigating, so length is secondary. Seven of the eight reached the 2^(free) atom count on the first part, then abandoned that sample space on the later part and asserted the outcome was a uniform random permutation, reading off 1/n; several equated the requested bottom slot with the item moved last, and two explicitly computed a small case that contradicted 1/n yet kept 1/n anyway. The revision therefore names the uniform-random-permutation phrase as the trap, adds that many step sequences collapse to one ordering and some orderings are unreachable, keeps the shared free-choice atom set and the last-in-first-out orientation, routes slot-occupancy events through a short prefix, and makes a small-case enumeration a veto that overrides any formula.

records.mutation: front-load commit-then-verify, add deviant-entry arithmetic recheck and evaluate-don't-expand coefficient extraction
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 1 of 8; the seven failures all ran to the 16384-token cap without stating any result. Three distinct sinks were visible: one rollout wrote the reduced instance with a wrong power, produced an off-pattern rational, and never questioned that single arithmetic slip; two abandoned already-verified small cases to compute one low-order coefficient of a 2004-factor product via elementary symmetric and harmonic sums, then looped on sign errors; another oscillated over how many conditions the shrunken system carries after letting one symbol be both index and exponent. The lone success committed to the signed factorial shape after two exact small cases. The revision therefore leads with commit-then-verify, routes a deviant table entry to an arithmetic recheck rather than a new theory, and forbids expanding a long product to read off a coefficient.

records.mutation: keep the train-safe opening and small-cases clause verbatim; upgrade the exact-arithmetic sentence to also prescribe factoring out common structure and choosing a fraction-clearing scaling, and make the closing check a substitute-back-into-the-givens check instead of a bare recheck
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored 1, so train is saturated and every gain must come from transfer. Round 8's kept edit (small-cases/invariant plus exact arithmetic) is the only mutation in nine rounds that raised transfer, while five wholesale rewrites or scope/divisibility additions each cut train or transfer, so I again preserve the train-carrying opening verbatim and only sharpen the general tail. Rollouts remain very long (10k-21k chars, 32-69 adversative pivots each) and the visible waste is arithmetic churn plus self-rereading: the student recomputes the same divisor and per-unit quantities many times and audits its own prior lines instead of the problem statement. So the tail now prescribes two concrete, domain-neutral economies: factor out common structure and rescale to clear fractions before grinding, and close by substituting back into the given numbers.

records.mutation: reframe the sum/difference step as a general symmetric-data lever, require the given numbers to stay on the right-hand side, and generalize the abort guard into one rule that any contradiction reached (degenerate center or parity objection) is a slipped line rather than refutation of the structure
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct, finishing in 4.5k-13k tokens by committing to the shared-center antisymmetric pair and solving via sum and difference. The single failure reached that exact form, then zeroed the given numbers when adding the two supplied values, got a degenerate center, and read that as proof the structure was impossible; it then manufactured a second self-refutation by arguing the inner/outer sign parity forbade odd k, and spent the remaining budget naming coefficients and expanding the degree-nine composition until the cap. The revision therefore keeps the proven centered core but makes retaining the given numbers explicit and collapses the abort guidance into one general rule: any contradiction met inside the structure is a slipped line to recheck, never grounds to abandon it. Wording is also compressed so the hint is shorter than the incumbent.

records.mutation: pin the scope of a block-onto-block step (not pairwise swaps) and make the row trace the explicit authority that overrides any hand-built index map
records.subagent_summary: 3 of 8 scored. Two failures never disputed the row trace but mis-scoped a step, reading a block-onto-block move as pairwise swaps inside the block; that halves the small-case counts and produced a clean but off-by-one exponent. The other three built an index map by re-applying each stage to the already-moved index, got a map that was not one-to-one (several inputs sharing one image), and when the map clashed with their own row trace they defended the map, looping on 'this is confusing' until the token cap. The incumbent warns about bijectivity in the abstract, so the revision instead pins the scope of a block move up front and makes the row trace the explicit authority that kills any map disagreeing with it, plus a terser commit clause to stop cap overruns.
